page: Vultr vcg-a16-12c-128g-32vram is a dedicated GPU-accelerated server instance featuring two NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs with a combined 32 GB of VRAM. The compute architecture is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz, delivering 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. System memory consists of 128.0 GB of RAM, translating to 10.67 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 700 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard CPU and memory operations, with a single-core stress-ng score of 1754.67 and a multi-core score of 21080.54. The system demonstrates strong memory bandwidth, reaching 1191.06 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 102.38 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For specialized workloads, the dual NVIDIA A16 GPUs deliver top-tier LLM inference speeds during prompt processing, achieving 8665.1 tokens per second on a 135M model and 613.27 tokens per second on a 7B model. Text generation speeds are also notable, reaching 32.35 tokens per second on a 7B model.

This instance offers a balanced resource density for GPU-accelerated workloads that require significant memory capacity without needing high-end compute cores. The combination of 128 GB of system RAM and 32 GB of total VRAM makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for medium-scale machine learning inference, data science pipelines, and virtual desktop infrastructure. However, the 2.0 GHz CPU clock speed and average single-core performance suggest it is less suited for CPU-bound sequential processing, making it best utilized for parallelized GPU workloads, LLM inference, and database operations.
